sentences.text: Wayside communications for Greenvale Metro are organized around continuous train radio coverage and a separated safety data backbone that carries vital movement authority traffic.
The Wayside Radio Access Network is sometimes called Saffron in radio survey records, but this document uses Wayside Radio Access Network as the canonical name.

The Wayside Radio Access Network provides overlapping cell coverage through stations, tunnels, crossovers, and depot approach tracks so that the Train Radio Modem can maintain a stable session during normal operation.
Radio sites are engineered with sector overlap at station throats and interlocking approaches because these locations combine frequent braking, switching, and train-to-wayside message activity.
The Train Radio Modem maintains the active bearer used by the Atlas Onboard Controller and reports radio quality changes before the session reaches the minimum design margin.
Handover is planned as a make-before-break event where practical, with the old radio path retained until the new path has accepted the session and passed basic message checks.
If radio quality degrades faster than predicted, the onboard equipment falls back to the last validated movement authority rules rather than accepting unverified wayside data.
The Safety Data Communication Network carries vital messages between zone controllers, interlockings, and approved interfaces using deterministic routing and monitored latency limits.
The Safety Data Communication Network is physically and logically separated from maintenance and passenger information traffic to reduce exposure to congestion and non-vital configuration changes.
Cryptographic Key Management Appliance supports the authentication framework used on the safety data paths and is managed under controlled access by authorized technical staff.
North District Zone Controller is sometimes called Marble in legacy boundary diagrams, but this document uses North District Zone Controller as the canonical name.
South District Zone Controller is sometimes called Orchid in commissioning notes, but this document uses South District Zone Controller as the canonical name.
North District Zone Controller supervises the northern main line, the northern turnback, and the approach to East Junction Interlocking within its configured limits.
South District Zone Controller supervises the southern main line, the southern turnback, and the approach to West Junction Interlocking within its configured limits.

The boundary between North District Zone Controller and South District Zone Controller is defined by track section ownership, radio coverage overlap, and the point at which a train authority must be reissued by the receiving zone.
At a zone boundary, the Atlas Onboard Controller confirms train position from the Dual Channel Odometer before accepting the next authority source.
The receiving zone validates route state, train identity, and the expected boundary track section before extending authority beyond the transfer point.
East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking report switch state, track occupancy, and route locking status to the responsible zone controller through vital interfaces.
Wayside supervision compares interlocking indications, train position reports, and radio session state to detect inconsistent conditions before they can affect service.
When the comparison detects a mismatch, the affected authority is withheld or shortened until the condition is resolved under the applicable operating rule.

Metro Operations Control System displays zone status, radio coverage alarms, and train supervision states so that Line Traffic Controller can manage service without direct intervention in vital logic.

Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives non-vital summaries of radio and network health, which allows Signal Maintenance Engineer to investigate degraded coverage trends without connecting to the vital channels.
Wayside Radio Access Network sends the Radio Handover Audit File after each configured reporting interval.
Voice Dispatch Console remains available as an operational communication path, but it is not used as a substitute for safety data messages or zone controller validation.
Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges only the permitted interface indications with the supervising wayside systems, and its state is not allowed to override movement authority logic.
Passenger Information Gateway and Service Timetable Server may receive selected service information, but those non-vital outputs are isolated from the command paths used for train protection.
